# Tuning acceptance thresholds (2015–2025 real NFL)

**Status: proposed 2026-11-08 — awaiting JR's sign-off (CLOSE_OUT_CHECKLIST P0-2).**
**Generated by:** `python3 -m engines.tuning.decision_targets` → `data/tuning/decision_targets.json` and `.md`
(git-ignored). Re-run with `--refresh` when the nflverse cache is stale. **The module is the source of truth**;
if this file and the module disagree, the module wins — re-run it and update this table.

---

## 0. The two audits (2026-11-08)

Two numbers in the first draft looked wrong to JR. Both were traced to a definition, not a bug.

### 0.1 Trades: 81/season vs the ~14 you'd expect

The first draft counted **all** trades (median 90/season). That is correct as an annual total, but it is not the
number Mu's weekly engine is competing with: 83% of NFL trades happen in March free agency, the draft, and the
September cutdown week. Split by date, against each season's game calendar:

| Season | 2015 | 2016 | 2017 | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **In-season** (Week 1 → season end) | 6 | 5 | 8 | 11 | 18 | 13 | 13 | 19 | 15 | 18 | 21 | **147** |
| Offseason (Mar, draft, Sept cutdown) | 46 | 45 | 73 | 82 | 84 | 58 | 78 | 74 | 75 | 68 | 75 | 758 |
| All | 52 | 50 | 81 | 93 | 102 | 71 | 91 | 93 | 90 | 86 | 96 | 905 |

**Reconciliation with JR's 155:** our 147 differs by 8 over eleven seasons. Three definitional choices account
for it:

1. **Window start.** "First game → last game" (147) excludes the **44 trades made in the September cutdown week
   before Week 1** (2015–2024). Start the window on September 1 instead and the total becomes **191** — the
   largest single lever, worth ~30%.
2. **Multi-team trades.** One 2021 trade involved four teams (`trade_id` 2019 season). A source that counts
   team-pairs rather than trade events scores it as 3–6 trades instead of 1.
3. **Season assignment.** nflverse assigns a trade to the season it affects; a March 2015 trade is `season 2015`,
   while a calendar-year count would put it in the 2014 offseason. Only January has any cross-boundary trades
   (4 in total across the window).

Neither our 147 nor a 155 is wrong; **the definition has to be fixed before it becomes a gate**. The module
reports both windows, and the gate below uses Week 1 → season end, because that is when `run_week` runs.

### 0.2 Career length: the famous "~3 years"

The first draft measured career span as `last_season − rookie_season + 1`, which gave a median of 7 for the
"established" cohort and looked far too long. It was measuring years *since debut*, including years out of the
league, and conditioning on players who had already survived.

Measured properly — **distinct seasons on a season roster with an active status** (ACT/RES/DEV/PUP/SUS/RSN/NWT),
using nflverse rosters 1999–2025:

| Population | n | mean seasons | median |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Players with ≥1 active season (careers ended 2015–2024) | 5,306 | **4.36** | 4 |
| …plus players whose only roster appearance was CUT | 6,802 | **3.40** | 2 |
| Drafted only | 2,234 | **6.0** | 5–6 |
| Undrafted only | 4,226 | **2.0** | 1–2 |

**The quoted ~3-year figure is the all-comers mean including cut-only players: 3.40.** It is a real number, but
it describes a population dominated by undrafted churn (65% of roster appearances). Drafted players — which is
what a draft class produces — average ~6 seasons, roughly double.

**Which one Mu should hit is a design question, not a data question.** Mu's population is whatever its draft
classes and free-agent generation put on rosters. The arithmetic constraint is:

```
mean career length  ≈  (roster slots) / (new players entering the league per season)
```

For example, 32 teams × 53 active + practice squads ≈ 2,200 slots. A 224-pick draft class alone implies a mean
career near 10 years; adding ~300 undrafted entrants brings it to ~4. So **the target cannot be set without
first measuring Mu's inflow** (drafted + generated UDFAs per season). That measurement is P3-06a below; until it
exists, the drafted cohort (mean 6.0, median 5–6) is the defensible default, with the all-comers 4.36 as the
floor and 3.40 only if Mu deliberately models a large camp-body population.

---

## 1. How a gate is scored

| Rule | Applies to |
|---|---|
| **Band** — observed 2015–2025 min–max per season. Passes when Mu's value is inside it. | per-season counts (coach changes, trades) |
| **Median ± tolerance** — Mu's median within the stated tolerance of the real median. | distributions (career length, retirement age) |
| **Rate ± relative tolerance** — within ±20% relative (e.g. 24.9% → 19.9–29.9%). | rates (team movement, rookie usage) |
| **3-season average** — decision counts are noisy in one season; compare the mean of three consecutive simulated seasons, then check each is inside the band. | every per-season count |
| **No silent pass** — a metric with no data in Mu's output is a **fail**, not a skip. | all |

A gate is only trustworthy once the **measurement** exists in the Mu database. The "Mu source" column names the
table; if it is empty the run fails with "not measured", which is the correct outcome.

| RB | 3 / 3.9 | 5 / 5.1 | 2 / 2.8 | 5% |
| WR | 3 / 3.7 | 5 / 5.4 | 2 / 2.7 | 6% |

### A3. Head-coach changes

| Metric | 2015 | 2016 | 2017 | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 | Band |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|

Derived from `home_coach`/`away_coach` on every regular-season game, so it is exact rather than reported.

- **Mu source:** `coach_tenures` (`start_season`/`end_season`) and `coaching_carousel` firings.
- **Primary suspect:** `engines/coach_hot_seat.py` thresholds; `owner_patience` config once shadowing.

### A4. Trades

| Metric | Band 2015–2025 | Median |
|---|---|---|
| **In-season** (Week 1 → season end) — **the gate for `run_week`** | **5–21** | **13** |
| Offseason (March, draft, September cutdown) | 45–84 | 74 |
| All trades, all year | 50–102 | 90 |
| Trades involving a player, all year | 49–102 | 81 |

- **Gate:** 3-season mean of in-season trades inside **5–21**; no single season above 30 or below 3.
- **Mu source:** `gm_trade_proposals` with `status = 'APPROVED'` (or `EXECUTED`), filtered to the regular season.
  Offseason-stage proposals are compared to the offseason band separately.
- **Primary suspect:** `gm_trade_engine` weekly volume constants, `MAX_BLOCKBUSTERS`, `--talk-stall`.
- **Definition settled (JR, 2026-11-08):** the cutdown week counts as **preseason**, so the gate is the
  Week 1 → season-end window (147 over the window) and cutdown trades sit in the offseason band. Do not use the
  September-1 definition (191).

### A5. Players changing teams (free agency + trades + cuts)

Band **17.9%–26.5%** of players with ≥8 games in both seasons, median **24.9%**, about **194 players a season**.

- **Gate:** Mu's rate within ±20% relative of 24.9% over a 3-season mean.
- **Mu source:** `player_season_transitions` where `status = 'MOVED'`.
- **Primary suspect:** `free_agency_engine` acceptance bar and counter steps; `contracts_engine` market values;
  cap growth.
- **Note:** total churn, not free agency alone; break down by `transactions.type` if the total is right but the split is not.

### A6. Draft by round (2015–2021 classes)

| Round | n | median career games | median wAV | share with 2+ started seasons |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 223 | 95 | 35 | 85% |
| 2 | 224 | 84 | 23 | 65% |
| 3 | 270 | 76 | 15 | 48% |
| 4 | 267 | 56 | 8 | 34% |
| 5 | 261 | 45 | 6 | 31% |
| 6 | 284 | 28 | 2 | 15% |
| 7 | 252 | 18 | 1 | 11% |

- **Gate:** round 1 within ±10 points of 85%; each later round within ±10 points; the monotonic decline must hold.
- **Mu source:** `draft_selections` + `player_seasons` starts and games.
- **Primary suspect:** `engines/scouting_value.py` and the rookie OVR distribution — not the drafting AI.

### A7. Rookie usage

Skill positions with recorded stats (linemen have no stat line and are excluded): **n = 2,326**, median **9**
games, **56%** with 8+ games, **36%** with 12+.

- **Gate:** shares within ±10 points; median within ±2 games.
- **Mu source:** year-1 games from the game/stat tables.
- **Primary suspect:** `depth_chart_engine` `close_score_window`; `development_opportunity` config.

## 3. B. Gates from the existing tuning stack

**Supersim baseline (JR, 2026-11-09):** the installed `Mu Base` already carries **Sabos FranchiseMod 1.3**, which
tunes 157 `supersim_*` assets (tackle chances, injury, fatigue, play time, run/pass/punt/FG play) against the last
three real seasons. So the supersim question is not "tune from vanilla" but **"does the installed mod already
pass?"** A supersim pass is: measure one simulated season with `Mu Base` active against these gates; if it
passes, **no supersim tuning is done at all**. If it fails, tuning starts from the **running Sabos values**, never
from vanilla.

| Metric | Gate | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Progression backtest MAE on 2035→2036 | ≤ 1.15 (current 1.134) | `engines/tuning/progression_fit.py` |
| 90+ OVR count vs the 2036 shape, 5 sim seasons | within ±5% of 144 | `--simulate 5` |
| Mean league OVR vs 78.13 | within ±0.3 | same |
| Per-season stat score | no stat more than **2 band widths** out; overall ≤ baseline | `engines/tuning/compare.py` |
| Worst-10 stats | each improves or holds vs the pre-tuning baseline | `compare` report |
| Sim noise | two baseline seasons within 10% of each other before iterating | P4-05 |

## 5. D. Rejected as gates

Three quantities that look like they should be targets but are not. They are still **reported** — they are just
not allowed to pass or fail a tuning run.

1. **Win-loss records, playoff seeds, award winners.**
   These are *outputs* of every engine at once, so they can't tell you which engine to fix: a team that goes 4-13
   might have bad drafting, bad contracts, bad coaching, bad progression, or just a bad quarterback. They are
   also enormously noisy — a single season's champion is close to a coin flip among the top eight teams, and
   award voting is discretionary in the real league too. **What covers them instead:** the league-shape gates
   (90+ count, mean OVR, position spreads) and the per-stat bands in `compare`, which decompose the same output
   into pieces you can act on. Records are still checked for *sanity* (no 0-17 or 17-0 clusters), not scored.

2. **Free-agent dollars per season** (total spend, average AAV, guarantees).
   This is a derived quantity: cap growth, the market-worth curves, contract structure and the number of
   qualifying free agents all move it, so two very different engines can land on the same total. It is also
   dominated by a handful of top-of-market deals, which makes it high-variance. **What covers it instead:** the
   team-movement rate (17.9–26.5% of established players changing teams), which measures whether the market
   *functions*, plus the contract-policy plan's own comparison report for the money side. Revisit only if FA
   spending looks wrong on inspection.

3. **Retirement announcement timing.**
   Mu decides retirements at one offseason stage by design; the real league has no single moment — players
   announce after the season, at the combine, in March, or not at all until a roster is filed. Matching the
   calendar would add scheduling complexity for no realism gain, and it would fight the `retirement` feature's
   one-decision-per-offseason rule. **What covers it instead:** retirement *age* and *career length* (A1, A2),
   which are what a reader actually notices.

---

## 6. E. What a failure means

A failed gate is a **bug report against a specific engine**, not a mandate to nudge a constant until the number moves.

| Failing gate | First place to look |
|---|---|
| Career length too short | `progression` wear/aging, then `retirement_policy` base rate |
| Career length too short *and* drafted players wash out | the **draft/UDFA inflow** — not enough new players, so the league over-retires |
| Career length bimodal | `progression` band spread — the middle is not developing |
| Too few 90+ players over 5 seasons | progression `league_term` and `upkeep`, not retirement |
| Coaches never fired / fired constantly | `coach_hot_seat` thresholds, `owner_patience` config |
| In-season trades far from 5–21 | `gm_trade_engine` volume and `--talk-stall`; check talks open at all |
| Team movement too low | `free_agency_engine` acceptance bar; cap growth |
| Round 1 and round 7 look the same | `scouting_value` / rookie OVR distribution — fix before AI tuning |
| Rookies never play | `depth_chart_engine` `close_score_window`; `development_opportunity` |

Record the failing gate, measured value, engine changed and re-measured value in the tuning ledger (P6-03).

## 7. Decisions taken and still open (P0-2)

### Settled by JR, 2026-11-08

1. **Trade definition — cutdown week is preseason.** In-season is **Week 1 → season end**: 147 trades over
   2015–2025, **band 5–21, median 13**. The September cutdown week counts as preseason and sits in the
   offseason band (45–84). A gate never uses the September-1 definition.
2. **Career-length population — drafted cohort for now.** Gate on the **drafted** median (5–6 seasons across
   groups), not the all-comers 3.40. The all-players figure stays in the report as the floor and as the number a
   broadcaster would quote. **Revisit after P3-06a** (Mu's own draft/UDFA inflow), which is what actually decides
   which population Mu can produce.
3. **Tolerances:** median ±1 season (±1.5 QB/K/P); shares ±10 points; rates ±20% relative.
4. **Averaging:** per-season counts pass on a 3-season mean, and each season must also sit inside the band.
5. **§4 scope:** blockbusters, holdouts and the P3-06a inflow measurement are pre-2026; GM and coordinator
   changes are deferred to a post-2034 pass.
6. **Retirement population:** the drafted median, matching A1.

Consequences applied throughout this document: A1's headline gate is the drafted column; A2 uses the drafted
median (all players retained as reference); A4's gate is the Week 1 → season-end window.
